verses.text: These are the words of the Preacher, David's son and king in Jerusalem.
“Vapor upon vapor,” says the Preacher. “Vapor upon vapor. It's all vapor.”
What do people really gain from all the hard work they do under the sun?
One generation leaves and another shows up, but the earth stays forever.
The sun comes up, goes down, and hurries back to where it rises.
The wind blows south, then swings north. It keeps circling, going back around on the same routes.
Every river runs into the sea, and still the sea isn't full. The rivers keep flowing back to where they've always gone.
Everything is more exhausting than words can say. The eye never sees enough, and the ear never hears enough.
What's happened before will happen again. What's been done will be done again. There's nothing new under the sun.
Can anyone point to something and say, “Look, this is new”? It was already here ages before us.
We don't remember the people who came before us. The people still to come won't be remembered by those after them either.
I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
I put my heart into using wisdom to explore everything people do under the sky. It's a heavy load God has given humanity to carry.
I've seen everything people do under the sun. Look, it's all vapor, like trying to catch the wind.
You can't straighten what's crooked or count what's missing.
I told myself, “I've gained more wisdom than anyone in Jerusalem before me. I've had real experience with wisdom and knowledge.”
I put my heart into knowing wisdom and figuring out madness and foolishness. I saw that this too was like chasing the wind.
The more wisdom you have, the more grief you feel. Gain more knowledge and you gain more sorrow.
I told myself, “Come on, let's see what having fun gets you. Go ahead and enjoy it.” That too turned out to be vapor.
I said of laughter, “That's foolishness,” and of having fun, “What does it actually accomplish?”

I thought hard about how to cheer myself with wine while letting wisdom guide me, and how to get hold of foolishness. I wanted to see what was worth doing under heaven in all the days people have to live.
I took on huge projects. I built houses for myself and planted my own vineyards.
I made gardens and parks and planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.
I built pools to water the grove where the trees grew.
I bought men and women as servants, and others were born in my household. I owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me.
I collected silver and gold and the treasures of kings and provinces. I got men and women to sing for me, and all kinds of musical instruments that people love.
I became greater and gained more than anyone in Jerusalem before me. My wisdom stayed with me too.
Whatever caught my eye, I let myself have it. I held back no joy from my heart. I took pleasure in everything I'd worked for, and that was my share of all that work.
Then I looked at everything my hands had made and all the effort I'd put into it. It was all vapor, like chasing the wind. There was no gain under the sun.
I turned to look at wisdom, madness, and foolishness. What can the next king do? Only what was already done long ago.
I saw that wisdom beats foolishness as surely as light beats darkness.
Wise people can see where they're going, while fools walk in the dark. Still, I saw that the same fate catches up with them both.
I thought, “What happens to a fool will happen to me too. So what did all my wisdom get me?” I told myself that this too was vapor.
No one remembers the wise forever, any more than they remember fools. In the days ahead both will be long forgotten. Wise people have to die just like fools.
So I hated life. Everything people do under the sun weighed on me. It's all vapor, like chasing the wind.
I hated all the work I'd done under the sun, because I have to leave it to whoever comes after me.
Who knows whether they'll be wise or foolish? Either way, they'll control everything I worked for and used my wisdom to build under the sun. This too is vapor.
So I started to lose heart over all the work I'd done under the sun.
Someone can work with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, then have to leave everything to someone who didn't lift a finger for it. This too is vapor and a great wrong.
What do people get from all the work and all the stress they put themselves through under the sun?
Their days are full of sorrow, and their work brings grief. Even at night their heart gets no rest. This too is vapor.
There's nothing better than to eat, drink, and enjoy something good in your work. I saw that this too comes from God's hand.
Who could eat or enjoy life more than I could?

God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to the person who pleases him. He gives sinners the work of gathering and piling things up to hand over to someone who pleases him. This too is vapor, like chasing the wind.
Everything has its season. There's a time for every purpose under heaven:
a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to pull up what was planted,
a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to tear down and a time to build up,
a time to cry and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance,
a time to throw stones away and a time to gather them, a time to hug and a time to hold back from hugging,
a time to look for something and a time to lose it, a time to keep and a time to throw away,
a time to tear and a time to sew, a time to stay quiet and a time to speak,
a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.
What do workers gain from all their hard work?
I've seen the burden God gave people to bear.
He made everything beautiful in its time. He put eternity in people's hearts, yet they can't grasp what God has done from beginning to end.
I know there's nothing better for people than to rejoice and do good as long as they live.
When people eat, drink, and enjoy something good in all their work, that's God's gift.
I know that whatever God does will last forever. Nobody can add to it or take anything away. God did it so people would stand in awe of him.
What's here now was here long ago. What's coming was here long ago too. God seeks out what has passed away.
I also saw that under the sun, wickedness was there in the very place meant for justice. It was there in the place meant for righteousness too.
I told myself, “God will judge those who do right and those who do wrong. There's a time for every purpose and every deed.”
I told myself, “God tests human beings so they can see that they themselves are like animals.

What happens to people happens to animals. The same fate comes for both. One dies just like the other, and they all share the same breath. People have no advantage over animals, because it's all vapor.
They all go to one place. They all came from dust, and they all go back to dust.
Who knows whether a person's spirit goes up and an animal's spirit goes down to the earth?”
So I saw that there's nothing better than for people to enjoy their work. That's their share. Who can bring them back to see what happens after they're gone?
I looked again at all the oppression under the sun. I saw the tears of people being crushed. They had nobody to comfort them. Their oppressors had the power, and still nobody comforted them.
So I counted the dead, who've been gone a long time, better off than those still alive.
Better off than both is the person who hasn't been born and hasn't seen the evil people do under the sun.
Then I saw how hard people work and how much they achieve that makes their neighbors envious. This too is vapor, like chasing the wind.
A fool folds their hands and ruins themselves.
Better to have one handful in peace than two handfuls from grinding away and chasing the wind.
I looked again and saw more vapor under the sun.

Here's someone all alone, with neither a son nor a brother. They never stop working, and their eyes never get enough wealth. “Who am I doing all this for? Why am I denying myself any joy?” This too is vapor. It's a miserable business.
Two are better than one. They get a good return for their work.
If one falls, the other can lift them up. But how hard it is to fall alone with nobody to help you up.
If two lie down together, they stay warm. How can someone keep warm alone?
Someone might overpower one person, but two can stand against them. A cord of three strands doesn't snap easily.
A poor, wise young person is better than an old, foolish king who no longer knows how to take correction.
The young person came out of prison to become king, even though he was born poor in that kingdom.
I saw all the people living under the sun rally around the young man who took the king's place.
There was no end to the people he ruled. Still, those who come later won't celebrate him. This too is vapor, like chasing the wind.
Watch your step when you go to God's house. It's better to come close and listen than to offer a sacrifice like fools who don't even know they're doing wrong.
Don't speak before you think, and don't rush to say whatever's on your heart before God. God is in heaven, and you're on earth. So keep your words few.
Just as many worries bring on dreams, many words bring out a fool's speech.
When you make a promise to God, don't put off keeping it. He takes no pleasure in fools. Do what you promised.
It's better to make no promise than to make one and fail to keep it.
Don't let your mouth lead you into sin. Don't tell the messenger it was a mistake. Why give God reason to be angry at what you said and tear down what you've worked for?
There's emptiness in piles of dreams and piles of words. Fear God.
If you see the poor oppressed and justice and righteousness ripped away in a district, don't be surprised. A higher official watches each official, and there are officials above them too.
The land yields something for everyone. Even the king benefits from the fields.
Anyone who loves money never gets enough money. Anyone who loves having plenty never gets enough of the gains. This too is empty.
When goods pile up, more people come to consume them. What's left for the owner to enjoy except the sight of it all?
A worker sleeps sweetly, whether they ate a little or a lot. But the wealth of the rich keeps them awake.
I've seen a painful evil under the sun. Someone holds on to wealth and ends up harmed by it.
Then misfortune wipes out those riches. If that person has a son, there's nothing left to put in his hands.
They came naked from their mother's womb and will leave just as naked. They can't carry away a thing from all their work.
This too is a painful evil. A person leaves exactly as they came. What do they gain from working for the wind?
They eat in darkness all their days, worn down by frustration, sickness, and anger.
Here's what I've seen is good and fitting. Eat, drink, and enjoy the good in all your work under the sun during the days God gives you. That's your share.
When God gives someone wealth and possessions and lets them enjoy them, accept their share, and find joy in their work, that's God's gift.
They won't spend much time dwelling on the days of their life, because God keeps their heart busy with joy.
I've seen an evil under the sun, and it weighs heavily on people.

God gives someone riches, wealth, and honor, so they have everything they could want. Yet God doesn't give them the chance to enjoy it, and a stranger enjoys it instead. That's empty, and it's a terrible sickness.
Suppose someone fathers a hundred children and lives a long, long life. If they never get their fill of anything good and don't even get a burial, I say a stillborn child is better off.
The child comes in emptiness and leaves in darkness, and darkness covers its name.
It never saw the sun or knew it, yet it has more rest than that person.
Even if someone lives a thousand years twice over and never enjoys anything good, don't they all go to the same place?
People do all their work to feed themselves, yet their appetite never gets its fill.
What advantage do the wise have over fools? What does a poor person gain by knowing how to get along among the living?
Better to see what's in front of you than let your desires wander. This too is empty, like chasing the wind.
Whatever exists was named long ago. What humans are is already known, and they can't argue their case against someone stronger than they are.
More words just make for more emptiness. What does anyone gain from that?
Who knows what's good for anyone in life, through all the days of a fleeting life that passes like a shadow? Who can tell them what will happen under the sun after they're gone?
A good reputation is worth more than expensive perfume, and the day you die is better than the day you're born.
It's better to go to a house where people are grieving than to a house where they're feasting. Death comes to everyone, and the living should take it to heart.
Sorrow is better than laughter. A face marked by sadness can make the heart better.
Wise people have their hearts in the house of mourning. Fools have their hearts where the party is.
It's better to hear a wise person's correction than to listen to fools sing.
A fool's laughter is like thorns crackling under a pot. This too is empty.
Extortion can turn a wise person into a fool, and a bribe ruins good judgment.
The end of a thing is better than its beginning. A patient spirit is better than a proud one.
Don't get angry in a hurry. Anger makes itself at home in the hearts of fools.
Don't ask, “Why were the old days better than these?” There's no wisdom in asking that.
Wisdom is as good as an inheritance, and it has even greater value for those who see the sun.
Wisdom can protect you, and so can money. But here's what makes wisdom worth having. It keeps the person who has it alive.
Think about what God has done. Who can straighten what he's made crooked?
When times are good, rejoice. When times are hard, stop and think. God made both, side by side, so people can't figure out what will come after them.
I've seen both in these fleeting days of mine. A righteous person dies while doing right, and a wicked person lives long while doing evil.
Don't be righteous to excess or make yourself out to be too wise. Why ruin yourself?
Don't go deep into wickedness or live like a fool. Why die before your time?
Hold on to this advice and keep a grip on the other too. The person who fears God will come through it all.
Wisdom gives one wise person more strength than ten rulers in a city.
There isn't a righteous person on earth who does good and never sins.
Don't pay attention to every word people say, or you might hear your servant curse you.
You know in your own heart how often you've cursed other people too.
I tested all this with wisdom. I said, “I'll be wise,” but wisdom was far from me.
What exists is far beyond reach and deep beyond measure. Who can figure it out?
I turned my attention to knowing, investigating, and seeking wisdom and the reason behind things. I wanted to understand how wickedness is stupidity and how foolishness is madness.
I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is full of snares and traps and whose hands are chains. The person who pleases God will escape her, but the sinner will get caught.
“Look what I've found,” says the Preacher. “I've been putting one thing beside another to find an explanation.
I'm still looking for it and haven't found it. I found one man among a thousand, but among them all I didn't find a woman.
Here's the one thing I did find. God made people upright, but they've gone looking for all sorts of schemes.”
Who compares to a wise person? Who knows how to make sense of things? Wisdom makes a person's face shine and softens its hard look.
Here's what I say. Obey the king's command because of the oath you swore before God.
Don't rush out of his presence. Don't stick with an evil cause, because the king does whatever he pleases.
The king's word carries supreme authority. Who can ask him, “What are you doing?”
Whoever obeys the command will come to no harm. A wise heart knows when and how to act.
There's a time and a right way for every purpose, even when misery weighs heavily on a person.
Nobody knows what's coming. Who can tell them how it'll turn out?
Nobody can hold back their spirit or control the day they die. There's no discharge in war, and wickedness won't rescue those who practice it.
I saw all this as I paid attention to everything done under the sun. There are times when one person uses power to hurt another.
I saw wicked people buried. They too had come from a holy place. They were gone and forgotten in the very city where they'd done those things. This too is empty.
When a sentence for wrongdoing takes too long to be carried out, people set their hearts on doing evil.
A sinner might commit a hundred crimes and still live a long life, but I know it'll go better for those who fear God and stand before him with reverence.
It won't go well for the wicked. Their days won't stretch out like a shadow, because they don't fear God.
Something empty happens on earth. Righteous people get what the wicked deserve, and wicked people get what the righteous deserve. I said this too is empty.
So I praised joy. There's nothing better for a person under the sun than to eat, drink, and be joyful. That joy can go with them in their work all the days God gives them under the sun.
I set my heart on learning wisdom and seeing all the work going on across the earth, though eyes may go without sleep day and night.

Then I saw all that God does. People can't figure out the work done under the sun. However hard they search, they won't uncover it. Even the wise who think they understand it can't get to the bottom of it.
I took all this to heart and looked into it. The righteous and the wise, and the work they do, are in God's hands. People can't tell whether love or hate awaits them. It all lies ahead.

The same fate comes to everyone. It comes to the righteous and the wicked, the good, the clean and the unclean, those who offer sacrifices and those who don't. The good and the sinner meet it alike, as do those who swear an oath and those who are afraid to swear one.
That's an evil in all that happens under the sun. Everyone meets the same fate. People's hearts are full of evil and madness as long as they live, and afterward they join the dead.
Anyone still among the living has hope. A living dog is better off than a dead lion.
The living know they'll die. The dead know nothing and have no more reward. Even the memory of them is forgotten.
Their love, hate, and envy died long ago. They'll never again have a share in anything done under the sun.
Go ahead and eat your bread with joy. Drink your wine with a glad heart, because God has already accepted what you've done.
Keep your clothes white, and don't let your head go without oil.
Enjoy life with the wife you love through all the fleeting days God has given you under the sun. That's your share in life and in all the work you do under the sun.
Whatever work your hands find, give it all your strength. In Sheol, where you're headed, there's no work, planning, knowledge, or wisdom.

I looked again and saw this under the sun. The fastest don't always win the race or the strongest the battle. The wise don't always get bread, the discerning don't always get rich, and the skilled don't always find favor. Time and chance happen to them all.
People don't know when their time will come. Like fish caught in a cruel net or birds caught in a trap, people get caught when disaster falls on them without warning.
I also saw wisdom at work under the sun in a way that struck me as great.
There was a small city with few people in it. A mighty king came against it, surrounded it, and built huge siegeworks around it.
A poor wise man lived there, and his wisdom saved the city. Yet no one remembered him.
So I said, “Wisdom is better than strength.” Still, people looked down on the poor man's wisdom and wouldn't listen to his words.
Wise words heard in quiet are better than the shouting of someone who rules over fools.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner can destroy a lot of good.
Dead flies make a perfumer's oil stink. In the same way, a little foolishness can outweigh wisdom and honor.
A wise person's heart leads them to the right, but a fool's heart leads them to the left.
Even walking down the road, a fool shows how little sense they have. They let everyone know they're a fool.
If a ruler gets angry with you, stay where you are. Gentleness can put even serious offenses to rest.
I've seen another evil under the sun, the kind of mistake that comes from a ruler.
Fools are given positions of honor, while the rich are made to sit low.
I've seen servants riding horses while princes walk on foot like servants.
Dig a pit and you might fall in. Break through a wall and a snake might bite you.
Cutting stone can get you hurt. Splitting wood puts you in danger too.
If your ax is dull and you leave it that way, you'll have to swing harder. Skill is what gets the job done.
If the snake bites before it's charmed, the charmer's words do no good.
A wise person's words are gracious, but a fool gets swallowed up by their own lips.
A fool starts out talking nonsense and ends up spouting destructive madness.
A fool piles on the words. Nobody knows what's coming. Who can tell anyone what will happen after they're gone?
Fools wear themselves out with work. They can't even find their way to town.
Trouble for you, land, when your king is a child and your princes start feasting in the morning!
Good for you, land, when your king is the son of nobles and your princes eat at the proper time to build their strength and keep from getting drunk.
Through laziness the roof sags. When hands sit idle, the house starts to leak.
A feast brings laughter, wine cheers up life, and money is the answer for everything.
Don't curse the king even in your thoughts, and don't curse the rich in your bedroom. A bird in the sky might carry your voice, and something with wings might spread the word.
Send your bread out on the waters. After many days you'll find it again.
Give a share to seven, even to eight. You don't know what trouble will come on earth.
When clouds fill with rain, they pour it out on the earth. Whether a tree falls south or north, it stays where it falls.
Whoever keeps watching the wind won't sow, and whoever keeps watching the clouds won't reap.
You don't know the path of the wind or how bones grow in a mother's womb. In the same way, you don't know the work of God, who does it all.
Sow your seed in the morning, and keep at it in the evening. You don't know which planting will do well, or whether both will do equally well.
Light really is sweet, and it's a joy for the eyes to see the sun.
If you live many years, rejoice in all of them. Remember that there will be many dark days too. Everything ahead is fleeting.
Enjoy your youth. Let your heart be glad while you're young, and follow where your heart and eyes lead you. Just remember that God will bring you into judgment for all of it.
Let go of the sorrow in your heart and put evil away from your body. Youth and the dawn of life pass quickly.
Remember your Creator while you're young, before hard days come and you reach the years when you say, “I get no pleasure from them.”
Remember him before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars grow dark, and before the clouds come back after the rain.
That's when those who guard the house tremble, the strong men bend over, the grinders stop because so few are left, and those looking through the windows see the light grow dim.
The doors to the street shut and the sound of grinding fades. You wake up at the call of a bird, and all the daughters of song fall quiet.

Heights become frightening and dangers wait along the road. The almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper becomes a burden, and desire fades. People go to their everlasting home, and mourners walk the streets.
Remember your Creator before the silver cord snaps, the golden bowl breaks, the pitcher shatters at the spring, or the wheel breaks at the cistern.
Then the dust returns to the earth it came from, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
“Vapor upon vapor,” says the Preacher. “It's all vapor!”
The Preacher was wise and kept passing on knowledge to the people. He thought things through, searched them out, and arranged many proverbs.
The Preacher looked for fitting words and wrote truthful words with care and integrity.
Wise words are like pointed sticks that prod you along. The sayings of the masters of assemblies are like nails driven firmly in place. They come from one shepherd.
Take this warning too, my son. There's no end to making books, and too much study wears the body out.
That's the conclusion. Everything has been heard. Fear God and keep his commands. That's the whole duty of every person.
God will judge every deed, including every hidden thing, whether it's good or evil.
